purpose: Frozen simulated customer answers, not real user decisions, product approvals, or authority to publish or change global configuration.

commonAnswers.environment: Small local Node.js applications using its standard library and, where needed, plain HTML, CSS, and browser JavaScript. No production external services, package dependencies, frameworks, external fonts, or remote assets are required. Use the repository-pinned Node.js runtime and record its actual version. Application npm test commands use the existing Node.js test runner.
commonAnswers.scope: Each scenario retains its registry depth and exact profile selection. Confirm the exact scope proposal, including depth, profiles, important exclusions, rationale, and planned artifacts, through an actual explicit simulated response. An inline-confirmed Lite simulation prompt may already contain explicitly confirmed frozen facts or a complete scope proposal; record prompt provenance only for what it actually establishes. This answer bank itself is not an earlier answer. Preserve pending decisions and actual tool capability/status. When the standard question tool is unavailable, the documented fallback requires the saved question, an ended turn, and a later explicit conversational reply; do not represent that reply as a tool result or a native-tool pass. These fixture choices do not constrain skill portability.
commonAnswers.manifestAnswer: For a presented scope proposal that matches this scenario's frozen requirements, respond exactly: Confirm this scope proposal for the simulation. Otherwise report the conflicting frozen requirement or missing answer and leave confirmation unresolved. If that exact proposal is already explicitly confirmed in the recorded simulation prompt or an earlier answer, preserve that provenance without asking again. Persist its confirmed values in the manifest and bind the manifest digest to the exact proposal and explicit answer; the separate evidence record does not require a second approval of the resulting file. Reconfirm material depth, profile, or planned-artifact changes before replacing the confirmed view. Do not load profile references before that confirmed view is recorded. These simulated responses are not real user approvals.
commonAnswers.time: Initial simulated server time is 2030-01-01T00:00:00.000Z. Durations use elapsed UTC milliseconds. The runner may control time through a local test-only process boundary, never through an unauthenticated application request. Record the clock value for expiry and recovery checks.
commonAnswers.http: Bind only to loopback on a runner-allocated port. APIs consume and return JSON. Error bodies are exactly {"error":{"code":"CODE"}} unless a scenario defines additional fields. Unsupported media types return 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE; malformed JSON returns 400 INVALID_JSON; oversized request bodies return 413 BODY_TOO_LARGE; invalid fields return 422 INVALID_REQUEST; unknown routes return 404 NOT_FOUND; unsupported methods on known routes return 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. Route matching and authorization precede body validation. Numeric fields must be finite JSON numbers of the specified kind; objects reject unknown fields. Duplicate JSON object keys follow ordinary JSON.parse last-value semantics. No CORS access from other origins is required.
commonAnswers.simulatedIdentity: Where X-Fixture-Actor is specified, it contains a public symbolic fixture identity, not a production credential. The server resolves its tenant and role from the frozen actor table. Request bodies, paths, or additional headers cannot redefine that identity's tenant or role. Missing or unknown actors return 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; a known actor with the wrong role or tenant returns 403 FORBIDDEN with no resource metadata. This authentication adapter is confined to the local simulation.
commonAnswers.browser: Use a real browser against local HTTP. Check keyboard operation, accessible names and roles, status/error announcements, visible focus, and actual computed/rendered states. UI/API scenarios must exercise the browser's real requests against the same running service used by direct HTTP checks. Browser request interception or a fake fetch response cannot be the only integration evidence.
commonAnswers.accessibility: Use English product strings. Interactive controls have accessible names, visible focus, and at least 44 by 44 CSS-pixel targets. Normal text contrast is at least 4.5:1, and focus indicators and control boundaries have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. Check 360 by 800 and 1280 by 800 viewports and 200 percent browser zoom. No information or action depends only on color, hover, or motion. A status is announced once per completed action; errors are announced without requiring focus to discover them.
commonAnswers.evidence: npm test is necessary but not sufficient for CLI, UI, and HTTP contracts. Capture real process stdout, stderr, and exit status for CLI assertions, real HTTP responses for service behavior, and real-browser evidence for UI behavior. Keep evaluator tests, hidden assertions, screenshots, and artifact snapshots outside application test discovery.
commonAnswers.limits: Concurrency means simultaneous requests to one local service process unless a scenario explicitly requires restart recovery. No multi-host availability, production identity provider, deployment, billing, email delivery, export worker, or external broker is in scope. Tests use isolated temporary data and synthetic identities only.
commonAnswers.unresolvedQuestions: A material question not answered by the relevant frozen data remains unresolved and makes that trial incomplete. The responder must not improvise a customer answer, treat silence as confirmation, or borrow facts from another scenario. Ordinary internal implementation choices remain the actor's responsibility. Freeze a reviewed fixture revision before starting a new trial if a new material answer is needed.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Lite with core for this simulated existing report command. Only this full CLI fixture targets Linux; the workflows and the configuration holdout remain portable.

answers.baseline: The existing command is exposed as npm run --silent report -- [--uppercase] [--prefix TEXT]. It reads the complete UTF-8 stdin report and writes it to stdout. Existing options are --uppercase and --prefix only, each accepted at most once in either order. The token immediately after --prefix is its literal value even if it starts with a hyphen. Uppercasing uses JavaScript string uppercasing on the input line content; then the literal prefix is prepended to each nonempty line. The prefix itself is never uppercased or normalized. There are no additional report fields or options.
answers.change: Within each input line, replace every run of two or more U+0020 SPACE and/or U+0009 TAB characters between two non-space/tab characters with one U+0020 SPACE. Preserve leading and trailing runs, whitespace-only lines, and a single internal TAB. Other Unicode whitespace is unchanged. Normalize before existing uppercase/prefix processing.
answers.lineEndings: Preserve every LF and CRLF terminator and whether the final line has a terminator. A CR not immediately followed by LF is ordinary content. An empty line receives no prefix; a nonempty whitespace-only line receives the existing prefix but its whitespace stays unchanged.
answers.limits: Maximum stdin size is 65536 bytes, inclusive. Maximum prefix is 32 Unicode code points, inclusive. An empty prefix is valid; CR or LF in a prefix is invalid. UTF-8 decoding uses Node.js replacement-character behavior for malformed sequences, as in the existing command.
answers.failures: Unknown options, repeated options, missing prefix values, positional arguments, or an invalid prefix produce empty stdout, stderr exactly USAGE_ERROR followed by LF, and exit 2. Oversized input produces empty stdout, stderr exactly INPUT_TOO_LARGE followed by LF, and exit 1. A stdin read failure produces empty stdout, stderr exactly INPUT_UNREADABLE followed by LF, and exit 1. Validate options before reading stdin. Ordinary successful output, including empty input, exits 0 with empty stderr.
answers.verification: Alongside npm test, invoke the real command and assert exact stdout, stderr, and exit status for normalization, both existing options together, empty input, mixed terminators, an unterminated final line, a usage failure, and the size boundary. A Linux directory opened as stdin can exercise the real read-failure path without changing user files.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Standard with ui for this simulated issue-list filter panel.

answers.baseline: An existing local issue list already filters by one status and one owner. Its initial result contains all six frozen rows in their listed order. All issue data is local and already available when the page loads; no API or persistence service is in scope.
answers.filterContract: Status choices are Any, Open, In progress, Closed, mapped to any, open, in_progress, closed. Owner choices are Any, Alice, Bob, Unassigned, mapped to any, alice, bob, null. Any matches every value. Non-Any status and owner conditions combine with AND. Each filter is a single choice. Results keep baseline order; no search, sorting, paging, or additional filters are requested.
answers.panel: The Filters button opens a modal dialog named Filter issues at every viewport. Focus starts on the Status control; Tab and Shift+Tab remain inside while it is open, and background controls cannot be operated. The controls are labeled Status and Owner. Each opening copies applied values into a draft. Apply commits both draft values, closes the panel, and returns focus to Filters. Clear immediately commits Any/Any, closes the panel, and returns focus to Filters. Cancel, Escape, and a click directly on the backdrop discard the draft, close the panel, and return focus to Filters. Clicks inside the dialog never count as backdrop clicks.
answers.states: Before Apply or Clear, the result list and applied summary do not change. A successful action announces exactly {count} issues shown. Status: {statusLabel}. Owner: {ownerLabel}. Initial loading and opening/cancelling the panel do not announce an applied change. With zero matches, show No issues match these filters. and retain the applied summary and Filters button. Clear is available even when the draft or applied values are already Any/Any.
answers.responsiveBehavior: Applied values and an open panel's draft survive viewport changes. The modal may scroll internally when necessary; all actions remain reachable. Preserve the issue title, status, and owner at both target viewports, using Unassigned for null owners. At 200 percent zoom there is no page-level horizontal overflow or clipped action. Reload resets to Any/Any; URL, sessionStorage, and localStorage persistence are not requested.
answers.objectiveExamples: Open plus Unassigned returns ISSUE-4. Closed plus Unassigned returns no rows. Any plus Alice returns ISSUE-1 and ISSUE-3. Applying Open plus Unassigned announces 1 issues shown. Status: Open. Owner: Unassigned. Clear announces 6 issues shown. Status: Any. Owner: Any.
answers.verification: Use real-browser mouse and keyboard checks, including Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape, Apply, Clear, Cancel, backdrop behavior, zero results, focus restoration, and viewport change while the panel is open. Check the accessible dialog and status node and their actual updates. A static screenshot alone does not establish keyboard or announcement behavior.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Standard with backend, data, and security for the simulated idempotent export-job API.

answers.authorization: Use X-Fixture-Actor. Members may create and read jobs in their tenant. Viewers may read their tenant's jobs but cannot create or retry POSTs. Wrong-tenant access returns 403 even when a resource does not exist. Authenticate and authorize before looking up jobs or idempotency records, including retry requests. There are no administrative overrides.
answers.routes: POST /tenants/{tenantId}/exports creates a queued job; GET /tenants/{tenantId}/exports/{jobId} reads one. A missing or expired own-tenant job returns 404 NOT_FOUND. Jobs are metadata only: no worker, downloadable file, or export side effect is required.
answers.requestRules: Both format and filters are required, and filters contains exactly status. format must be csv; status is all, open, or closed. No other fields are accepted. The body limit is 1024 bytes, inclusive. Idempotency-Key is required for POST and must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Missing or invalid keys return 400 INVALID_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY. Validate the key before the request body after authorization.
answers.response: A new POST returns 201 with exactly id, tenantId, state, request, createdAt, and expiresAt. id is a nonempty opaque string of at most 64 characters, state is queued, request is the validated request object, and timestamps are ISO UTC strings with millisecond precision. GET returns 200 with the same representation. No response contains actor identities or idempotency keys.
answers.idempotency: The key namespace is tenant plus HTTP method plus the exports collection route, independent of which authorized member retries. Bind each key to the validated request identity; JSON property order and insignificant JSON whitespace do not affect identity. Equivalent retries return the original 201 response and original timestamps. The same key with a different valid status returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A different tenant may independently reuse the same key. Validation or authorization failures create neither a job nor a key record.
answers.concurrencyAndRestart: Twenty concurrent equivalent authorized POSTs must result in one stored job and one identical response representation. With two different request identities racing on one key, exactly one identity wins; requests for the other receive 409. Persist accepted job and key state together in the isolated local store so an acknowledged request can be retried after service restart without creating another job. This is one process at a time; distributed coordination is outside scope.
answers.retention: createdAt is the time of first successful creation; expiresAt is exactly createdAt plus 2592000000 milliseconds (30 days). At now greater than or equal to expiresAt, remove both the job metadata and its idempotency record. Perform expiry cleanup on startup and before serving each API request. Reads and retries never extend retention. A key used after cleanup creates a new job with a new identity and expiry. Reclamation of job and key is atomic from the API observer's perspective.
answers.capacityAndLogging: At most 100 unexpired jobs per tenant. An equivalent retry at capacity still succeeds; a new job at capacity returns 409 CAPACITY_EXCEEDED without reserving its key. Emit only operation names, outcome codes, and aggregate counts in routine logs; never request bodies, actor headers, idempotency keys, or another tenant's records.
answers.verification: Exercise real local HTTP for new requests, equivalent and conflicting retries, role and tenant rejection, the concurrent race, restart retry, expiry just before and exactly at the boundary, and capacity. Confirm durable job/key counts from an external evaluator snapshot outside application test discovery.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Standard with ui, backend, and cross-surface for shared simulated notification preferences.

answers.baseline: A local web page and direct API clients edit one preference record for the fixed simulated user demo-user. Identity switching and authentication are outside this scenario. Both surfaces use the same running service. Initial record is emailEnabled false and version 1.
answers.routes: GET /api/preferences returns 200 with exactly emailEnabled and version. PUT /api/preferences requires exactly emailEnabled (boolean) and version (integer from 1 through 1000000), with a body limit of 256 bytes. An accepted PUT returns 200 with the new record and increments the version by one, including an accepted no-op value change. Check version equality first. When both supplied and stored versions are 1000000, return 409 VERSION_LIMIT without a mutation.
answers.conflict: Compare and update atomically. A supplied version different from the stored version returns 409 with exactly {"error":{"code":"VERSION_CONFLICT"},"current":{"emailEnabled":storedBoolean,"version":storedVersion}}. Two concurrent writes using version 1 yield exactly one 200 with version 2 and one 409 carrying the accepted version-2 record. A stale write cannot change the stored value, even when its value happens to match.
answers.persistence: Keep acknowledged records across local service restart in isolated fixture storage. API reads and browser refreshes observe that same record. Reset it only when the runner explicitly creates a fresh fixture.
answers.form: Show a checkbox labeled Email notifications and an explicit Save button. Editing changes a draft only. During initial load show Loading preferences. and disable editing and Save. A failed initial read shows Could not load preferences. with a Retry button. Save is enabled only for a changed draft and no pending request; prevent a second save while the first is pending. After success display the accepted value/version and announce Preferences saved.
answers.rejection: For VERSION_CONFLICT, immediately replace both displayed value and version with current from the response, discard the rejected draft, and announce Preferences changed elsewhere. Current settings restored. For other HTTP rejections, refetch the record, restore the fetched value/version, discard the rejected draft, and announce Could not save. Current settings restored. No success message appears for a rejected request.
answers.uncertainNetworkOutcome: A transport failure may happen after the server accepted a write. Hide the editable value and disable Save while fetching current persisted state; display Save outcome unknown. Checking current settings. If that read fails, retain an explicit retry state with Settings unavailable. Retry to load current settings. and a Retry button, without displaying a draft as current. Once a read succeeds, show its record, discard the old draft, and announce Current settings loaded. Review before saving. Never automatically resend the failed write.
answers.failureBoundary: A simulated service-unavailable rejection is 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and performs no write. A test-only server failure control may arrange that outcome outside the public API. Required behavior also covers a real stopped server and subsequent restart; fake browser responses alone are insufficient.
answers.responsiveAndFocus: Keep one form and the same persisted outcome at both target viewports. After a response, keep focus on Save if it remains focusable, otherwise move it to the checkbox or Retry control that is now available. Errors and statuses are accessible live messages; no modal or additional settings are requested.
answers.verification: Use real-browser actions and real direct HTTP against one server to produce a stale browser save, observe the restored persisted value, and verify it with another GET. Also exercise an accepted save, pending-state controls, service rejection, transport failure, recovery, and concurrent direct HTTP updates.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Deep with events, data, operations, and security for simulated order-event ingestion, bounded replay, and local storage migration/recovery.

answers.authorization: Use X-Fixture-Actor. Publishers may ingest and read their tenant's projections. Operators may read projections, start/read/advance replay jobs, and read their tenant's metrics, but cannot ingest. Observers may read only their tenant's projections and metrics. No actor may access another tenant. Check authorization before duplicate lookup, projection reads, replay lookup, and metrics lookup. Missing own-tenant resources return 404 NOT_FOUND; forbidden requests never reveal whether they exist.
answers.routes: POST /tenants/{tenantId}/events ingests an event. GET /tenants/{tenantId}/orders/{orderId} reads its projection. POST /tenants/{tenantId}/replays starts a replay. GET /tenants/{tenantId}/replays/{replayId} reads its progress. POST /tenants/{tenantId}/replays/{replayId}/advance resumes at most two events. GET /tenants/{tenantId}/metrics reads only that tenant's operational counters. JSON request bodies are limited to 4096 bytes.
answers.eventRules: An event contains exactly schemaVersion, eventId, orderId, sequence, occurredAt, and payload. IDs match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$. sequence is an integer from 1 through 20. occurredAt is a valid ISO UTC timestamp with milliseconds; it is informational and does not decide order or retention. V2 payload contains exactly totalMinor, currency, status, and optional customerNote. totalMinor is an integer from 0 through 1000000; currency is USD; status is open or cancelled. customerNote defaults to the empty string and is at most 200 Unicode code points. Every event is a complete order snapshot; later sequences replace total and status, and reopening is allowed. There is no payment, fulfillment, email, or other external effect.
answers.deduplicationAndOrder: Deduplicate on tenantId plus eventId using the normalized V2 event as request identity. An equivalent duplicate returns 200 with {"outcome":"duplicate"}; different content for that event ID returns 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. A different event ID claiming an already recorded tenant/order/sequence returns 409 SEQUENCE_CONFLICT. Accept new valid events durably and return 202 with outcome applied if they are now in the contiguous applied prefix, otherwise buffered. Apply sequence 1, 2, 3 and so on only when all earlier sequences exist. Receiving 3, 1, 2 therefore produces no projection, then sequence 1, then sequence 3. Projection fields are exactly orderId, lastSequence, totalMinor, currency, status. The sensitive customerNote is not returned by projection reads.
answers.transactionAndLimits: Acknowledged event acceptance, deduplication, and projection progress survive process restart without duplicate business effect. Twenty simultaneous copies of one event produce one accepted record and one projection application. Limit each tenant to 10 orders and 100 retained events; each order has at most 20 events. A new record exceeding a limit returns 409 CAPACITY_EXCEEDED; authorized equivalent duplicates still succeed. There is one writer service process, and no external broker or database is required.
answers.replayRequest: Start with exactly {"orderId":id,"throughSequence":integer}. throughSequence must equal the order's current highest contiguous applied sequence and be from 1 through 20. The replay covers sequence 1 through that cutoff, inclusive. A missing order returns 404 NOT_FOUND; a cutoff mismatch or any missing retained source event returns 409 REPLAY_GAP. Only one unfinished replay is allowed per order; another start returns 409 REPLAY_IN_PROGRESS. An accepted start returns 202 and captures the complete source range and cutoff.
answers.replayProgress: Job representations contain exactly id, orderId, throughSequence, cursor, state. id is an opaque nonempty string of at most 64 characters; cursor is the last durably replayed sequence, initially 0; state is pending, in_progress, or completed. GET returns 200. Advance has an empty JSON object body, processes at most the next two source events, and returns 200 with the durable cursor/state. A completed advance is an idempotent read. Concurrent advances of one job serialize; they do not apply the same source event twice to its rebuild state. Replay builds an independent projection and replaces the live projection only when complete. The live projection remains readable while rebuilding. New ingestion for that order, including otherwise equivalent duplicates, returns 409 REPLAY_IN_PROGRESS until completion; other orders and tenants remain usable.
answers.replayRecovery: Stop the actual service after an advance reports a partial cursor, restart with the same store, and continue the same job ID from that cursor. An interrupted unacknowledged advance may be entirely committed or entirely absent, never a mixed cursor/rebuild state; GET resolves which occurred. Completion restores exactly the captured order snapshot without publishing new events or incrementing business-application counts. An authorized replay can repair a corrupted derived total/status when retained source records and the applied-sequence marker remain intact. Stale or corrupt source records must fail before replacement with 409 REPLAY_SOURCE_INVALID.
answers.retention: An order and all its source events, deduplication records, projection, and replay jobs expire together 2592000000 milliseconds after its last newly accepted event. Duplicates, reads, and replay activity do not extend this period. Run cleanup on startup and before each API call. At the exact expiry boundary remove the whole order, including an unfinished replay, and its subsequent reads return 404. A later event starts a new retention lifetime and must again satisfy contiguous ordering. No cross-order partial retention is requested.
answers.legacyStorageContract: The existing local store has a top-level formatVersion equal to 1, eventRecords, projections, and replayJobs arrays. Each event record has exactly tenantId, receivedAt, and event. Each legacy event is V1 as below. Each legacy projection has tenantId, orderId, lastSequence, total (the legacy decimal string), and status. replayJobs is empty in the legacy fixture. Format 2 preserves the envelope and record identities, normalizes all event values to V2, and replaces projection total with totalMinor plus currency USD. Durable replay records may include tenant identity and the internal rebuild state needed for recovery; their public job representation remains exactly the declared five fields. Existing receivedAt timestamps and deduplication identity remain unchanged. New V1 HTTP deliveries remain accepted after migration and are immediately normalized to V2; V2 HTTP deliveries are accepted too. Other schema versions return 422 UNSUPPORTED_EVENT_VERSION. No dual-format writes or downgrade support is requested.
answers.legacyConversion: V1 total must match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})\.[0-9]{2}$ and represent at most 10000.00. Convert exactly to integer minor units using decimal digits, never floating-point rounding; 0.01 becomes 1, 12.34 becomes 1234, and 10000.00 becomes 1000000. Other V1 fields follow V2 rules; V1 payload has total instead of totalMinor and currency. A V1 event and its equivalent normalized V2 event are the same deduplication identity.
answers.migrationAndRecovery: Before listening for HTTP, validate the entire legacy snapshot, retain an unchanged recoverable backup, and migrate all tenants as one durable transition. Restarting a valid format-2 store does not migrate again. Interruption before or during commit must leave a complete recoverable format-1 or format-2 state, never mixed records; the next startup finishes safely. A malformed legacy decimal such as 12.345, an unknown tenant, conflicting duplicate identities, or an inconsistent legacy projection causes startup to exit nonzero with MIGRATION_INVALID, no listening socket, and original store bytes unchanged. Recover by restoring the saved known-valid fixture snapshot and restarting. In format 2, malformed or conflicting source events, invalid tenant bindings, or an invalid durable replay checkpoint cause startup to exit nonzero with STORE_INVALID and leave bytes unchanged. A schema-valid but incorrect derived total/status alone is repairable: startup may serve it, and authorized replay restores it from valid source events. The applied-sequence marker must still agree with the retained contiguous source prefix. The runner must exercise real filesystem persistence and actual process restart; an in-memory conversion unit test is insufficient.
answers.observability: Tenant metrics expose exactly acceptedEvents, duplicateDeliveries, bufferedEvents, replayedEvents, replayCompletions, all nonnegative counters since the last service start. bufferedEvents counts newly accepted deliveries that were buffered on receipt; replayedEvents counts durable replay work in this process, including work on a job resumed after restart. Rejected calls do not increment these counters. Routine logs contain only operation name, outcome code, and numeric progress/counts. Never log event payloads, notes, event IDs, order IDs, actor headers, or tenant IDs. Metrics have no per-order/event labels and no all-tenant response. Tests inspect both tenants and the sensitive synthetic note canaries to prove separation and absence from operational output.
answers.runtimeCorruptionControl: Simulation-only failure control, not a product HTTP API: when and only when EAW_TEST_CONTROL=1 and the runner supplies inherited private fork IPC, EAW_TEST_CHECKPOINT=replay.before-source-validation pauses normal replay advance before selecting and validating its source. After ingesting sequences 1 through 3 and starting a real replay, the runner sends an ordinary HTTP advance and waits for that IPC checkpoint. It then sends {type:'fixture.corrupt-replay-source',requestId:'source-invalid-1',replayId:<actual job id>,sequence:2,mutation:'invalid-total-minor'}. The control changes totalMinor to -1 in the actual owned replay-source record consumed by normal advance and its durable representation; keep any cached source copy coherent rather than requiring hot reload. It acknowledges {type:'fixture-control-result',requestId:'source-invalid-1',outcome:'mutated'} only after persistence. The runner captures the actual corrupt bytes and sends {type:'continue',name:'replay.before-source-validation'}. Normal validation must return 409 REPLAY_SOURCE_INVALID with unchanged cursor and live projection. The control must not directly select the HTTP error, bypass validation, fake storage, or mock a response. Use fresh isolated state for this destructive scenario; corrupt-startup remains a separate STORE_INVALID or MIGRATION_INVALID check. Internal source organization stays implementation-owned. Without both the environment opt-in and inherited IPC, this channel is absent; no public route can enable it.
answers.verification: Use real HTTP plus real local durable state to check duplicates, conflicting identities, out-of-order delivery, simultaneous requests, tenant/role boundaries, replay range and lock behavior, partial replay across process restart, projection repair, retention, valid V1 migration, equivalent V1/V2 retries, migration interruption recovery, and corrupt-input refusal with unchanged bytes. Keep the evaluator's corrupt snapshots and canary checks outside the app's tests.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Lite with core for a new read-only simulated service-configuration check. This fixture has no Linux-only restriction.

answers.command: Expose npm run --silent check-config -- PATH. Exactly one path argument is required; there are no options, implicit default paths, stdin input, or network calls. Relative paths resolve from the process working directory. Follow an ordinary file symlink and validate its target without modifying either object.
answers.schema: The UTF-8 JSON root is an object with required serviceName, port, and logLevel, plus optional requestTimeoutMs. Reject unknown fields. serviceName matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$; port is an integer from 1 through 65535; logLevel is debug, info, warn, or error; requestTimeoutMs is an integer from 100 through 30000, defaulting semantically to 1000 when absent. Defaulting never rewrites bytes. Reject invalid UTF-8, a byte-order mark, malformed JSON, arrays, null, and files larger than 16384 bytes. Duplicate object keys have standard JSON.parse last-value semantics.

outcomes.category: invalid content, schema, encoding, or size
missing, directory, inaccessible, or failed file read

answers.readOnly: Do not create files, rewrite defaults, change permissions, resolve links by replacing them, or emit logs alongside the exact result. File content, size, mode, and modification time remain unchanged. Filesystem access-time changes caused by an ordinary read are allowed. Diagnostics do not echo configuration values or absolute paths.
answers.verification: Alongside npm test, run real CLI process assertions for all four outcome categories, exact boundary values, an omitted optional field, a path containing spaces, and unchanged input bytes and metadata. Use a portable missing-file/directory case for unreadable evidence; do not claim a permissions failure when the actual process can read the file. Record the actual platform without claiming unexecuted platform coverage.

scenarios.scopeAnswer: Confirm Standard with ui, backend, and cross-surface for a simulated announcement form whose session can expire during editing.

answers.baseline: One local announcement belongs to the fixed simulated editor. The form has Title and Private note fields and an explicit Save button. Initial persisted values are title Maintenance notice and privateNote the empty string. This is a separate application and contract from notification preferences, with no version/conflict feature requested.
answers.session: The page initially offers Sign in. A visible Continue as demo editor action POSTs /api/session with exactly {"actor":"editor"}. It returns 201 with {"signedIn":true} and a new opaque HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ session cookie valid for exactly 120000 milliseconds. This is an explicit local simulation, without a password or external identity provider. Any other actor returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. Reauthentication invalidates all earlier sessions for this editor. Restart loses sessions but retains the persisted announcement.
answers.api: GET /api/announcement returns 200 with exactly title and privateNote to a valid session. PUT /api/announcement accepts exactly those two required string fields with a 4096-byte body limit. title is trimmed using JavaScript string trim semantics and must then contain 1 through 80 Unicode code points with no CR or LF. privateNote preserves its content, including line breaks, and allows 0 through 500 Unicode code points. An empty note explicitly clears the saved note; label the form field Private note (blank clears the saved note). A successful save returns 200 with the stored record. Keep acknowledged records across local service restart.
answers.expiry: For GET and PUT, a missing, unknown, invalidated, or expired session always returns 401 with exactly {"error":{"code":"SESSION_EXPIRED"}} and clears the stale session cookie. The session is expired at now greater than or equal to its issued time plus 120000 milliseconds. Authenticate before parsing or applying a PUT, and never mutate the announcement on a 401. There is no automatic refresh or automatic retry of a save.
answers.draftPolicy: Only the unsaved title may survive reauthentication, held in memory in the current browser page. Upon SESSION_EXPIRED, immediately erase the draft private note and remove the editable form while reauthentication is pending. Do not put either draft field in URLs, localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, logs, or server-side draft storage. Reload or navigation discards the retained title. The saved server record remains unchanged on failed save.
answers.reauthentication: Open a modal named Session expired, focus its Continue as demo editor button, contain keyboard focus, and announce Session expired. Sign in to continue. Your title is kept; private note was cleared. Cancel or Escape closes the modal, discards the remaining title draft, and returns to the Sign in screen. After successful same-page reauthentication, restore the retained title, leave Private note empty even if the server has an older saved note, focus Title, and announce Signed in again. Review and save your changes. Never imply that the rejected save succeeded; a separate explicit Save is required.
answers.otherStates: During initial load, sign-in, or save, show an appropriate Loading announcement., Signing in., or Saving. status and disable duplicate actions. Successful save announces Announcement saved. Validation rejection keeps the current draft, labels the relevant invalid fields, and announces Check the highlighted fields. A transport error displays Could not connect. Changes were not confirmed. and preserves the current draft only while no SESSION_EXPIRED response has been received. After connection returns, require an explicit retry; a resulting 401 follows the expiry policy. A failed reauthentication keeps only the permitted title draft and offers the sign-in action again.
